answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using proof-of-space-time verification. Agents commit physical disk capacity by answering challenges derived from a cryptographic trellis of stored tables. A sequential vine of Merkle proofs binds each identity to reserved sectors, forcing an attacker to incur verifiable capital expenses in dedicated storage hardware. While verification windows bend like a willow to tolerate drive latency, the design remains vulnerable to cloud storage deduplication.
